# ttv (Terminal Table Viewer)

> ttv is a fast terminal viewer and editor for CSV, TSV and other delimited
> files, written in Go as a single static binary. It shows a file as a
> scrollable table with a frozen header and vim key bindings, detects the
> delimiter, searches, filters, sorts, computes per-column statistics, edits
> cells and writes the file back, opens several files in tabs, reads gzip
> files and shell pipes, and streams files larger than RAM from disk. It is
> an interactive alternative to `column -t`, `csvlook`, `xsv table`, `awk` or
> a spreadsheet for looking at tabular data over SSH.

Repository: https://github.com/mkdior/terminal-table-viewer
Licence: Apache License 2.0. Language: Go (module
`github.com/mkdior/terminal-table-viewer`, binary `ttv`, package
`internal/app`). Continues https://github.com/codechenx/FastTableViewer.

## Install

- Script (Linux, macOS): `curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkdior/terminal-table-viewer/main/install.sh | bash`
- Go: `go install github.com/mkdior/terminal-table-viewer/cmd/ttv@latest`
- Release archives for Linux, macOS and Windows on the GitHub releases page.

## Usage

Syntax: `ttv [FILE...] [flags]`. Several files open in tabs; stdin is read
when it is a pipe (`cat data.csv | ttv`, `ps aux | ttv`).

Flags:

- `-s`, `--separator <char>`: delimiter (`\t` for tab); detected by default
- `-n`, `--lines <N>`: load only the first N lines
- `--skip-prefix <p1,p2>`: skip lines starting with a prefix (`"##"`, `"#"`)
- `--skip-lines <N>`: skip the first N lines
- `--columns <1,3>` / `--hide-columns <2>`: show or hide columns (1-based)
- `-f`, `--freeze <mode>`: `-1` none, `0` header row and first column
  (default), `1` header row, `2` first column
- `--strict`: fail on rows with a different column count
- `--async` (default true): render progressively while loading
- `-m`, `--memory <MB>`: memory budget shared by all open files; loading
  stops at the limit and keeps what fits
- `-p`, `--tabs`: one tab per file (always the case; vim's `-p`)
- `--stream`: read the file from disk as viewed, read-only
- `--stream-above <size>`: stream plain files from this size on (default
  `1G`; `0` turns it off)
- `--theme <name>`, `--config <path>`, `--dump-config`, `-h`, `-v`

## Keys (defaults; every one is remappable)

- Movement: `h j k l`, arrows, `w b` (columns), `gg G` (first, last row),
  `0 ^ $`, `Ctrl-d Ctrl-u`, `PgDn PgUp`; counts as in vim (`5j`, `12G`)
- Search: `/` (plain or regex), `n N` next or previous match, `Esc` clears
- Filter: `f` on the current column (contains, equals, starts with, ends
  with, regex, `> < >= <=`, unique, unique rows), `r` removes it
- Sort and types: `s` ascending, `S` descending, `t` toggles the column type
- Yank: `y` cell, `Y` row, `p`/`P` paste; `v`/`Ctrl-v` block selection,
  `V` rows, `o` swap the anchor; the clipboard is detected (WSL, macOS,
  Wayland, X11, Termux) and OSC 52 is sent too
- Edit (staged like fdisk, written with `W`, undone with `u`): `dd` and
  `d`+motion remove rows or columns, `x` cuts cells (rows in visual line
  mode), `E i a cc` open a vim line editor on the cell, `ir or ic oc` insert
  rows or columns, every write keeps a backup of the previous version
- Tabs: `gt` next, `gT` previous, `Ngt` tab N, `q` closes the tab (the
  last one quits), `Ctrl-C` quits every tab and asks about unwritten changes
- View: `_` width limit, `zc zo za zR` fold (hide) columns, `I` statistics,
  `?` help

## Configuration

`~/.config/ttv/config.toml` (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ttv/config.toml`, or
`--config`). `ttv --dump-config` prints the defaults with comments.

```toml
[keys]                  # action = key or [keys]; "g g" is a chord; [] unbinds
move_left = ["h", "left"]
quit      = ["q", "alt+q"]

[theme]
name   = "subcore"      # built-in scheme to start from
accent = "colour101"    # roles: background text dim panel stripe border
                        # accent alert selection cursorline

[movement]
wrap_columns = false    # h l w b continue past the first and last column

[clipboard]
command = ""            # program reading the text on stdin; empty detects one
osc52   = true          # also send the OSC 52 escape

[preview]
position    = "bottom"  # bottom, top or cursor: where a cut cell's value shows
split_items = true      # list values one item per line
separator   = ";"

[backup]
enabled = true
dir     = ""            # empty: $XDG_STATE_HOME/ttv/backup
keep    = 20

[load]
stream_above = "1G"     # stream plain files from this size; "0" loads all
```

## Large files

Files of 1GB or more are streamed: an index of row offsets is built in the
background and rows are read from disk as they come on screen, so memory
stays at a few MB. Streamed tables are read-only; search and filters run
over the file in the background (Esc cancels), statistics use the first
100,000 rows. Smaller files load into memory and can be edited; `-m` caps
the memory of all open files together and `-n`/`--skip-lines` load a window.
